Research That Drives the Future of Computing & Innovation
Program Overview
The Computing & Information Science Doctor of Philosophy program at UNO is a research-intensive, multidisciplinary doctoral program that prepares students to lead in the advanced computing and information technology field. Through close faculty mentorship and hands-on research in areas like artificial intelligence, data analytics, software engineering, and cybersecurity, students gain the expertise needed to drive innovation and succeed in competitive industry roles or research-focused careers.

Concentration Areas
Artificial Intelligence Concentration
This concentration builds advanced skills in intelligent systems, machine learning, and natural language technologies, preparing students to create AI solutions for complex computational problems.
Computing Systems Concentration
This concentration focuses on modern architectures, networks, and operating systems, equipping students to design secure, scalable, and high‑performance computing environments.
Human-Centered Computing Concentration
This concentration explores how people interact with technology, preparing students to design intuitive, research‑driven systems that improve user experience and digital engagement.
IT Project Management Concentration
This concentration strengthens expertise in information systems research and advanced project management, preparing students to lead complex IT initiatives and guide technical teams effectively.
Program Details
The program offers a flexible curriculum that allows you to shape your research path across computing, information systems, and informatics.
Partner with faculty on funded research projects
Gain experience through research assistantships
Access specialized labs equipped for advanced work
Work in areas like Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, and AI
Build presentation, publication, and collaborative experience
Collaborate across departments and industry partners. Pursue dissertation pathways aligned with your career goals.

The Ph.D. program maintains a structured annual progress review to support student success and ensure steady advancement toward degree completion.
Complete a yearly progress report with your faculty advisor
Document milestones, teaching outcomes, publications, and other achievements
Reports are evaluated by the Doctoral Program Committee (DPC)
DPC provides written feedback and identifies concerns
Failure to submit required reports can result in advising holds, loss of funding, or dismissal from the program
Students who are dismissed may petition the DPC to reapply by submitting a written explanation to the program director by the specified deadlines.
